analysis_summary: The snapshot (daily-20260704T224229Z) shows no top plays because core external feeds (injury report, roster verification, and slate lines) were unavailable or failed to parse. Public web evidence confirms that the primary sources needed by the model do exist and were actively publishing NBA roster/injury and odds information on July 4, 2026 — meaning the problem appears to be a local ingestion/parse/watchlist gating issue in the snapshot rather than an absolute absence of upstream data. However, sportsbooks and league sites also show active offseason and summer-league activity (roster moves, schedules, and live odds), so the snapshot’s statement that no slates/lines were available is contradicted by live public sources.
bottom_line: Public sources show the upstream data the model depends on (official NBA injury/transaction pages and sportsbook odds/schedules) were available on July 4, 2026. The snapshot’s 'no playable top plays' outcome therefore most likely stems from local ingestion/parse failures, missing roster verification feed, or the snapshot being placed into watchlist-only health-gate mode — not from an absolute absence of public injury reports or market lines. Evidence is mixed: authoritative feeds exist (ESPN/Rotowire, nba.com) and sportsbooks publish odds (DraftKings), so re-running the model after fixing the injury-parsing and roster verification ingestion (and confirming access to sportsbook/slate endpoints) is recommended. If you want, I can (1) fetch the specific injury/inactive status for any player(s) you care about for July 4–5, 2026, or (2) run a targeted check of the model’s data endpoints (injury API, roster feed, and sportsbook feed) to identify which ingestion step failed.
